claims.note: narrowed the descriptive positioning from a wholly verifiable history to change accounts checked against the artifact
expanded the strategic guardrails from four to five
added the disclosure-scope boundary for append-only history
split Who into requesting, producing, editing, and recording roles
explained why a scalar author field is insufficient
listed the minimum actor and attribution fields
prohibited attributing agent-produced work to a human owner
expanded the privacy risk heading to cover retention boundaries and access control
clarified that append-only does not mean recording all human or agent activity
defined ledger admission as the point where append-only semantics begin
introduced three logical disclosure scopes without requiring a full permissions system
defined ephemeral, private, and shared lineage
set one artifact as one disclosure boundary for portable v0
listed safe handling options for history excluded from the shared capsule
defined append-only redaction and the limits of revoking replicated plaintext
deferred fine-grained ACL and key management to server backends

context.why: The trust promise needed to distinguish verified changes from attributed context, and append-only history from indiscriminate recording or premature ACL complexity.
rejected: Fine-grained ACL and per-field encryption in portable v0 — turns the protocol into a key-management and permissions platform before handoff value is validated.
Silently deleting or rewriting an admitted shared event — breaks the trust property; correction and redaction must themselves be visible events.
